# Rules the script enforces (details)

Spec lock (T2) · REQ line changed since its test's last Green/Refactor ⇒ evidence stale (re-verify: `tdd refactor` for wording-only, `tdd red`/`green` for behaviour changes; so a new requirement means: edit spec first, then test) · Red before Green with identical test hash (its own annotated test + shared imports/data/helpers; sibling test bodies excluded) · hash-chained `.sdd/tdd.jsonl` · every REQ has a test, every annotation resolves · skipped checks ⇒ `INCOMPLETE` (exit 2), never PASS.

Every `@verifies` REQ of a test is hash-tracked · `approval: human` needs a lock on any tier; `--by` is normalized (trim/NFKC), so `" ai:x"`, `ai`, empty names cannot pass as a human · frontmatter tolerates CRLF, trailing `# comments`, quotes · `plan` warns about specs missing from `.sdd/plan.md` · a green/refactor run where every test was skipped is rejected · `gate --changed` keeps repo-wide trace errors and sees untracked dirs.

Lock drift: a lock made under T2/`approval: human` goes stale if the spec later drops either (AI approvers are refused; a human re-locks), and a deleted locked spec fails the gate until `approve retire <feature> --by <human>` · BOM/CRLF-normalized spec hashes, full-width (NFKC) `（deferred）`/REQ digits · the last test's hash region ends at its closing line, so appended tests/`main()` don't stale it · `gate --changed` always reports `unknown REQ` trace errors · conflicted ledger ⇒ `tdd merge-ledger` (union, dedupe, re-chain) · `approve prepare` writes `.sdd/prepare-shown.json`; `record` warns without it, and refuses generic human names (bot/user/ai…).

Human-approved specs: `approve record` stores the shas of the `@implements` files; a later change makes `gate` print a `!` warning "implementation changed since approval" (not a failure).

Not enforced (agent discipline): test quality, mutation, security review. Do not claim them.

## Wave-2b oracle and ownership refinements (#199–#205)
- Oracle closure includes Rust Unicode `#[path]` escapes/intervening attributes; C/C++ object-like literal include macros, compiler-forced includes and fragments of any extension; Java same-package support and `CsvFileSource` local resources/files; PHP same-namespace static/new class references; xUnit string collection definitions/fixtures; NUnit ancestor-namespace and assembly `SetUpFixture`; Julia literal/module-qualified and `joinpath(@__DIR__, …)` includes. Unsupported C/Julia/Java oracle expressions are refused rather than omitted; deleted local inputs invalidate evidence.
- Cargo source `include!` ownership preserves lexical modules. Shared annotations across executables are refused unless the runner chooses a target explicitly. Generic NUnit verdicts aggregate argument-suffixed TRX methods without accepting longer sibling methods.
- Java/PHP/C#/Julia generated subjects are annotated production before Red. Handwritten subjects need CODE/@implements before Red; later promotion cannot silently remove a protected oracle and receives a recovery diagnostic. See `stubs.md`.
- Git-less Rust stubs discover imported Cargo members; PHP readonly declarations retain impact edges. Julia character literals do not corrupt sibling isolation, and standard `Test` module aliases receive automatic nested-summary visibility. PHPUnit 13.4+ autodetection avoids its deprecated result-cache option.

## Review file schema
If `--review` is a file (e.g. `.sdd/review.md`) it must follow the schema from `$S review template <feature>` (or `--feature <feature>`; `review check <file> --feature <f>` also takes the feature positionally): one matching `spec: sha256:<hash>` header (12–64 hex chars, all supplied characters must match; legacy `spec <hash>` is accepted), `verdict: pass` (the template starts as `pending` and is rejected until edited), `open: <n>`; findings carry an explicit status (table cell, `- [ ]`, `state: open`, `**Open**`). A hash elsewhere in prose does not qualify. Explanatory suffixes such as `Open (awaiting fix)` remain Open. `open:` must equal the Open lines found and be 0. Validate with `$S review check <file> --feature <f>`.
Absolute and root-relative review paths, including paths with spaces, identify the same file and receive the same validation and subsequent hash freshness checks. Explicit absolute/path-shaped missing files are refused, not treated as summaries (#196).
`approve record --by ai:<reviewer>` requires `--review <path|summary>`; `ai:self` is refused; gate shows lock kind and review evidence.

## Red variants
- Stub Red: if the throwing stub is hit by a setup call rather than an assertion, Red is recorded weak with a warning. `tdd red <ID> --expect <text>` requires the failure output to contain the text (wrong-reason Red is rejected); Julia checks the selected target's failure diagnostics, not a sibling's message. `--allow-setup-red` accepts setup-origin evidence as-is.
- Flow-based ACT rule (r25d, TS/JS, Python, Rust): a stubbed call is the act, not setup, when its data flows into an assertion of the same test regardless of helper naming — its bound result (or an argument it fills) is the receiver of an asserted expression (`assert [1] == s.get()`, `assert.deepEqual(await s.get(), …)`, `o.getvalue()`), or the result is iterated and the loop variable is asserted (`for p in &s.polygons { assert!(..) }`, `for (const p of s.items)`). This also makes `new Store()` vs `registry()` shapes classify identically with and without `stubThrowingConstructors`. Conservative: a result that only feeds another call, is never asserted, or is bound by `with … as` (pinned setup, #292) stays setup. Not covered (skipped as risky): Red "fails with" text selection (assertion line vs cleanup/custom message), `match` arms via helpers, `assert.throws` predicate failures.
- Weak vs suspect (r24c, design 3.3): a weak Red whose only evidence is the name-based setup-vs-act heuristic is also recorded `suspect: true` in the ledger (additive; `weak` stays set, so old ledgers and gates behave as before). Load errors, `NAME = None` stubs, pytest fixture/ExUnit setup errors, C# type initializers, characterization and retest are high-confidence `weak`, not suspect. A suspect Red never blocks `tdd red`; it prints `! suspect Red … tdd red <ID> --allow-setup-red` (a command that is always accepted), and `gate` lists all suspect Reds in one place in the evidence line.
- New module tests: `tdd red <ID> --missing-module` accepts a Red caused by the test's own not-yet-created import (not weak).
- `tdd refactor --stale` re-verifies all tests whose shared implementation changed since their Green (#295).
- Data-only / characterization tests (e.g. a contract lock check) pass without any implementation, so `tdd red` rejects them; record them explicitly with `tdd red <ID> --characterization "<why>"` (stored as a weak Red and counted separately in the gate). Successful characterization/retest output says `test passed`, never `fails with`.
- Wrong test expectation found after Red: fix the test, then `tdd red <ID> --retest "<reason>"` (reason required; only if a Red/Green exists for the ID and the test changed since). The run may pass; recorded as a weak Red, then `tdd green` as usual. This is the supported path (#248): `tdd green` refuses a changed test file, and a plain `tdd red` on a now-passing test is rejected. This is the supported path (#248): `tdd green` refuses a changed test file, and a plain `tdd red` on a now-passing test is rejected.
- Node spec/TAP output must contain an executed result for the ID, not merely an ID-bearing filename. Skipped/TODO results (including TODO assertions that fail) cannot establish Red/Green/Refactor or characterization evidence; an all-skipped/TODO gate check is INCOMPLETE (#154). pytest collection errors and Julia top-level `LoadError`s are rejected as load errors. Julia whole-file runs reject a Red/Green attributed to a test whose own testset did not fail. `tdd red|green|refactor` accept several IDs; `--by` strips zero-width/format characters; an AI lock is stale if its cited review file is deleted or edited; T1 `approve record` is not lock-enforced.
- Legacy repos: `trace --baseline` snapshots errors to `.sdd/trace-baseline.json`; later trace/gate report only new errors (counted per message, so an added same-kind error is new) (`--changed` also limits to changed files).
- Human approval order: `approve prepare <feature>` (shows paths/hashes) → human reviews → `approve record <feature> --by <name>`. Record is refused without a prepare matching the current spec; after any spec/design edit, prepare again. The first implementation after approval refreshes the code baseline; later edits to `@implements` files are flagged.
- `tdd green` accepts a test whose content equals any earlier recorded Red (reverting a wrong test edit); other changes need a new Red. Test-file BOM/CRLF changes do not stale evidence.
- `impact <id|file>`: same-feature REQs are listed apart from other-feature REQs (`!`). Go resolves to files declaring the used symbols (package fallback), JS barrel files over-approximate, Python/Rust/Java/C/PHP resolution is heuristic. An unannotated file belongs to the features of its same-named / same-directory annotated files; a test file is labelled `test:`, not `impl:`. Rust `use name::..` resolves only against the crate with that Cargo package name; C quoted includes resolve relative to the includer first (then by path suffix), `<dir/x.h>` only when it names a project path, and `.h`↔`.c` pair by basename only in the same directory (or when unique). C# (`using`/namespace + mentioned type names, restricted to projects the importer's csproj references transitively via `ProjectReference`/`Directory.Build.props`; csproj, shared props and `.sln`/`.slnx` are graph nodes, so a changed csproj reaches its dependents; `bin/`/`obj/` are never scanned) and Julia (`include("..")`, `using .Mod`) have a basic import graph; other build-system edges are not modelled.
- Weak Red heuristic (setup vs asserted call) is best-effort: helper functions are scanned, and `step(..).unwrap();` or a bare call statement (`eng.run()`) right before assertions that call nothing else counts as the act; a helper whose result is asserted is not setup; `gate` lists the weak Red IDs (re-record with `tdd red <ID> --expect <text>` before implementing; after Green keep it weak or temporarily break the implementation). Rejected Red/Green and the `fails with:` reason prefer the assertion line (ctest `CHECK failed`, xUnit `Assert.X() Failure`/`Exception : msg`, JUnit `expected: <a> but was: <b>`, Julia `Expression:`). Use `--expect` / `--allow-setup-red` to override. #142 weak-Red details: .NET `Assert.X`/`CollectionAssert`/`StringAssert`/`.Should()` count as assertions; an asserted result may appear anywhere in the assertion (chained comparison, tuple, non-leading argument, `v.attr`, `helper(v)`) or via a variable derived from it (`got = [t for t in toks]`) — unless the same assertion calls other code; `Class.method` / `Class::method` / `Class->method` stub messages name the method; a Go `panic:` stub is attributed through the first non-runtime stack frame (`fails with:` shows the panic text); Rust `unimplemented!()` is attributed via the panic location; a C# static/type-initializer failure (`TypeInitializationException`) is always a weak (setup) Red. A stubbed call hidden in a helper that wraps the act (`mustAdd(t, e, ..)`) stays weak by design: re-record with `--expect <text>`.
- Runner verdicts (#143/#156): a timed-out run, or a crashed runner (termination signal, `Fatal Python error`, forked JVM `OutOfMemoryError`/`error in the forked process`, CLR fatal error, aborted test host), is REJECTED for Red, Green and Refactor, even with `--weak` (never a valid Red; never reported as "no test matched"). With several .NET test projects, the VSTest summary `Failed!/Passed! - ... Total: N` of one project counts as a match even if another prints "No test matches". Julia runs the whole file: a testset that is missing from the Test Summary because an earlier top-level testset failed is rejected as "never ran"; a passing testset is Green even when a sibling testset fails. For failing Red runs, `fails with:` falls back to NUnit `Expected is`, PHPUnit's first failure message and finally the last output line; rejected Rust runs keep the `assertion `left == right` failed` and left/right lines.
- `@id` suffixes must be uppercase; `CODE-X-001b` is reported as an invalid id, not as a duplicate.
- #301: `impact` on code also reaches REQs of projects whose `dependsOn` names the changed file's project (transitive); `gate --changed` runs (in full) the project check of a feature whose spec file alone changed.
- `gate --changed` warns (`!`) when changed files are imported by code/tests of another feature; their evidence is not re-checked, so run a full gate or `impact <file>`.
  The hint lists every affected feature and also fires on a spec-only change. `impact` resolves Python relative imports, PHP `use`, and skips TS type-only imports; its output is capped.
- Ledger writes take `.sdd/tdd.lock` (stale after 15s), so concurrent `tdd` runs no longer corrupt `tdd.jsonl`. Lone-CR (`\r`) line endings in spec frontmatter are accepted.
- `tdd refactor` warns when the test body changed since the last Green (no Red proves the new assertions); use `tdd red/green` if assertions changed. On T1 specs (#302) such a refactor is refused unless `--wording "<why>"` is given. The gate trace line lists deferred REQ IDs; TS compile/transform errors are reported as load errors. Record `approve` after the last spec edit: any later edit invalidates the hash.
- Dogfood-6 (#144–#146): a test's hash region ends at its own top-level construct for every test (not only the last), so a helper or a new `describe` placed between tests no longer stales the previous one; `tdd refactor` warns "test body changed" only versus the latest Green *or* Refactor. `impact` follows Python `from pkg import submodule`, Go methods-only files (via the receiver type), go.mod in a subdirectory (module path mapped to the directory), static JS/TS `import x from "x.json"` (JSON files are graph nodes as import targets), and does not call an unannotated file "same feature" when its directory holds several features. `trace` warns when a spec table's Test column lists an id that does not exist or does not `@verifies` that REQ. `projects[].dependsOn` accepts `./x`, `x\`, `x/`; `gate` warns for a path missing on disk. pytest is autodetected also from `conftest.py` / `tests/test_*.py`. Unknown flags exit 2 (`gate --changd`); `tdd <red|green|refactor> A B` validates all IDs before writing any ledger entry.
- Review files (#138): `Pending`, `Reopened`, `Unresolved`, `TODO`, `WIP`, `In progress`, `Blocked` count as Open (only Closed/Resolved/Fixed are resolved). `review check` exits 2 for a missing file, unknown feature or missing `--feature`; `approve record --by ai:x --review <path.md>` refuses a path that does not exist (a free-text summary must contain spaces).
- `gate` reports `--retest` Reds separately from characterization (`N retest: <IDs>`) (#139).
- A run where every test was skipped (node:test `ℹ skipped`, Go `t.Skip`, PHPUnit `Skipped:`/`Assertions: 0`/"did not perform any assertions", dotnet `Passed: 0, Skipped: n`) is rejected for Red, Green and `--characterization` (#140).
- Pytest skipped/xfail-only summaries (or `-qq` progress without a summary) cannot establish Red/Green/Refactor or characterization evidence (#156). A full gate check with only these outcomes is INCOMPLETE; a scoped check falls back to its full check. Mixed runs with genuine passing tests remain valid.
- Pytest `{idu}` resolves the annotated function's complete name, including descriptive suffixes; default `-k` selection excludes longer sibling names containing that name (#157).
- Python `--missing-module` accepts a missing dotted module explicitly imported by the test (including an absent parent), not an unrelated transitive dependency or a module already present in the project (#158).
- Python test hashes use syntax-parsed function boundaries: decorators (on either side of comment annotations), complete multiline signatures and docstrings belong to the test. Shared imports retain names and aliases; same-file helpers and oracle data outside test functions are conservatively hash-tracked, including trailing definitions (#159). Sibling test bodies are excluded. If Python parsing is unavailable, the whole file is protected. Unsafe legacy Python region/import-normalized hashes are no longer accepted: re-record Red/Green for old Python evidence.
- Go `impact` follows same-package production symbol dependencies as well as tests, module-root imports, promoted embedded methods and named/unnamed alias receivers. Local `replace` paths are resolved in the importing module's scope, retaining subpackage suffixes even when the replacement declares a different module path; symbol narrowing still excludes unrelated declarations (#160).
- Direct Go test runners request verbose target results: a package-level summary alone cannot establish Red, characterization, Green or Refactor. `TestMain` early exits without an executed target are rejected, even with `--weak`; build failures remain load errors (#161).
- Go annotated literal `t.Run` targets resolve to an exact anchored `parent/group/subtest` filter, including annotations inside callbacks or directly before `t.Run`. Verbose and JSON results must match that exact target: a passing subtest cannot borrow a failing parent/sibling's Red, and absent/skipped subtests provide no evidence (#162). Dynamically computed subtest names are not resolved; use a literal name or an annotated top-level test.
- Git-less roots (#163): manifest discovery, impact and C# project ownership use filesystem discovery. An unavailable Git status is not a clean tree: `gate --changed` prints a diagnostic and runs full evidence/checks.
- Exact attribution (#164): `{idu}` resolves the complete annotated Rust/C/Java/PHP/C# function/method, including descriptive suffixes. Direct Cargo runners use the module-qualified name with `--exact`; default CTest regexes and PHPUnit method filters are anchored (PHPUnit allows dataset suffixes); default VSTest filters use the qualified method with equality when resolvable and request verbose results. Parsed target results cannot borrow a longer sibling's failure or execution. Julia summaries use each table's own columns and token-exact IDs; a passing target stays Green despite a later sibling failure.
- Execution and crashes (#165/#167/#168): Gradle counts skips in its per-task summaries; CTest skipped/not-run and Julia broken-only or absent targets cannot provide Red, characterization, Green or Refactor. All-skipped, zero-test and Gradle NO-SOURCE-only full checks are INCOMPLETE even when the runner exits successfully; scoped checks fall back to their full check. CTest child signal exceptions (including SegFault) are crashes, rejected even with `--weak`/`--expect`. PHPUnit errors/failures before its assertion counter increments still count as execution; mixed passing/skipped provider rows remain valid.
- Shared oracles (#166/#170): Rust/Java/PHP/C#/C/C++ balanced function boundaries protect the test plus shared non-function data and transitively referenced same-file helpers, wherever defined. Annotated implementation and sibling test bodies are excluded; inline Rust protects its `#[cfg(test)]` region. Uncalled trailing functions (including C `main`) do not change the test body, even after a one-line test. Unparseable constructs conservatively protect the whole file. Unsafe legacy region hashes are no longer accepted for these languages; re-record old Red/Green evidence.
- Julia `@test_throws` marks the subject call as an assertion, not setup-origin weak Red (#169).
- Ownership and execution (#171–#173): Cargo metadata selects the owning package/executable and follows out-of-line `mod` declarations; outcomes stay scoped to that executable. Java default selectors include package/class identity, with exact Gradle events or fresh JUnit XML results. C# character literals cannot corrupt qualification. Zero-execution Cargo and skipped-only VSTest summaries reject evidence and make full checks INCOMPLETE; an executed .NET target is not erased by a sibling project's no-match message.
- Oracle protection (#174/#175): framework lifecycle callbacks (Java/PHP/C#), helpers referenced through shared C macros/callback data, case-insensitive PHP providers, and Julia shared/trailing oracles participate in the test hash. Julia excludes annotated sibling test bodies and implementation regions; old unsafe Julia hashes need fresh Red/Green.
- CTest (#177/#178): default selectors discover a unique exact method/ID registration, anchor its name, and reject missing/ambiguous registrations. A standard C assertion's attributable subprocess abort is strong Red, not a runner crash; unrelated signal exceptions remain rejected.
- Case identities (#179/#180): PHPUnit filters include newline-named datasets and recognize PHPUnit 12 `#index`/`@name` failure suffixes without matching longer sibling methods. NUnit `TestName` and MSTest `DisplayName` metadata identify custom case results. Direct Julia file runners enable verbose nested testset summaries through an include-time AST transform, without editing test source; custom runners must expose equivalent summaries themselves.
- External oracles (#181): Rust local test-support `mod`/`#[path]` and literal `include!`/`include_str!`/`include_bytes!` dependencies, and local C/C++ includes, are hash-tracked transitively with cycle protection. Dependencies marked as annotated production (CODE without TEST) are excluded; otherwise local include contents are conservatively protected. Dependency changes/deletion stale Green and refuse an old Red hash; old hashes that omitted these dependencies need new Red/Green.
- Rust glob impact (#182): local-crate `use crate_name::*`, grouped globs and module globs add conservative source/submodule edges rather than silently dropping downstream callers.
- Runtime identity and execution (#183/#185): Rust raw/byte raw strings cannot affect enclosing modules. Java nested classes use JVM `$`, C# nested classes/records use CLR `+`, and bare records retain their declaring type. Direct Maven/Gradle TDD requires fresh target XML/events even after a successful build. JUnit same-class overloaded methods are refused as ambiguous (use unique method names); a no-argument target cannot own another signature's dataset results. Direct .NET TDD selects the test's nearest owning csproj rather than running same-qualified methods across a solution; ambiguous ownership requires an explicit project.
- Declaration/lifecycle hashes (#184): inline/qualified JUnit annotations preserve method boundaries and sibling isolation. PHPUnit `Before`, `After`, `BeforeClass`, `AfterClass`, `PreCondition` and `PostCondition` attributes protect their callbacks, including qualified names and imported aliases.
- CTest helpers/registration (#186): standard C assertion aborts from reachable same-file helpers are strong target Red; unrelated helper diagnostics and sibling signal exceptions still do not excuse crashes. Unique method/ID registrations can use punctuation or underscore delimiters; the full registration is regex-escaped and anchored, excluding longer alphanumeric siblings.
- Julia evidence/runners (#187/#188): ID matching includes hyphens, so `TEST-X-001-OTHER` cannot supply execution for `TEST-X-001`. An explained changed-target `--retest` can record weak passing-target Red despite a failing sibling; normal Red/characterization still cannot borrow that sibling failure. Verbosity injection only rewrites compatible default testsets and direct file operands, never custom AbstractTestSet constructors or arguments after a custom launcher script. Custom testsets/launchers must expose observable target summaries themselves.
- Transitive local oracle closure (#189): the same cycle-safe traversal protects Rust modules/includes, C/C++ headers (quoted or angle-bracket, including bare local names), Java/PHP/C# local inheritance and support bindings, and Julia literal includes. Rust raw literals and nested `concat!` with `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` resolve to actual files; unresolved Rust include expressions explicitly refuse evidence. `#[path]` respects inline-module directories and ordinary out-of-line attribute bases. Deletion/change invalidates old evidence; CODE-only production files remain excluded. Cross-file support is conservative (whole dependency contents, not per-method slicing); local name ambiguities protect all candidate support files.
- Lifecycle ownership (#190/#195): Java composed/meta-annotations, qualified/aliased/Attribute-suffixed C# lifecycle attributes, and multiline/aliased PHPUnit attributes protect callbacks. Unknown Java helper annotations are conservatively protected. Same-file lifecycle callbacks apply to their declaring class, enclosing nested classes and locally resolved inheritance chain, not unrelated sibling classes. Private/protected PHPUnit helpers remain reachable oracles even when named `test_*`.
- Impact bindings (#191): Cargo path/package dependency aliases resolve in the importing package, and Julia `using`/`import` visits every comma-separated module before an optional colon import list.
- CTest results (#193): whitespace-bearing registrations retain their complete name through selection/results. Standard C++ assertion diagnostics may contain a return type and function signature; reachable target/helper aborts are strong Red, while unrelated helper aborts and genuine signal crashes remain rejected.
- Runtime method rows (#195/#197): default PHPUnit filters include the declaring namespace/class. Direct .NET runners select the owning project and write a fresh `.sdd/results/sdd-target.trx`; exact method filters aggregate **all** selected rows, including arbitrary runtime/constant display names. Constructed generic fixtures use a bounded class/method filter and require TRX method ownership; longer methods cannot lend results. Runners without generic method metadata explicitly refuse evidence. Non-generic custom runners without TRX retain console attribution (an exact qualified direct filter is required to aggregate arbitrary display names).
- Julia syntax/visibility (#198): keyword symbol literals such as `:begin` do not open blocks or absorb sibling hash regions. Direct-runner verbosity supports `Test.@testset` and `Test.DefaultTestSet`, without rewriting unrelated/custom macro or constructor types.

## Wave 3/4 dogfood-7 refinements (#213–#224)
- Oracle closure (#214/#219/#224): Python `conftest.py` files in the test's directory and every ancestor up to the root; JS/TS relative `import`/`export … from`/`require`/string-literal `import()` of local test-support files (test-like paths such as `test/`, `fixtures/`, `helpers/`, `*.oracle.*`) and local data (`.json/.csv/.txt/.yaml`); R `source("<literal>")` of test-support files, literal data paths read by the test (`read.csv`, `readRDS`, `readLines`, `test_path`, …) and testthat `helper-*.R`/`setup-*.R` beside the test. Annotated production (`@id CODE-`) and non-test-like production files are not oracles. Non-literal paths (`import(path)`, `source(paste0(...))`) are not resolved: keep those oracles inline.
- `gate --changed` with `projects` (#213/#222): when every changed file is inside nested projects only root checks that look like test runners (name or command contains test/spec/jest/vitest/pytest/mocha/unit) are skipped; workspace-wide root tooling (typecheck, lint, build) still runs. The skip message lists only the projects that actually changed.
- Rust (#217): `test x - should panic ... ok/FAILED` rows are attributed like ordinary rows. A cargo `process didn't exit successfully` caused by a signal or an exit status other than 101 (stack-overflow abort, `process::exit`) is a crashed host and is REJECTED for Red/Green even with `--weak`. Doctests cannot carry `@id` evidence (known limit: wrap them in a `#[test]`).
- `--retest` (#221): a retest that passes records a weak Red; when it replaces an earlier strong Red it prints a warning and `gate` reports how many retests superseded a strong Red. The strong Red is not silently re-credited (the changed expectation was never seen failing); to keep failing-Red evidence, temporarily break the implementation before `--retest`.
- Macro-declared tests (#217/#220/#223): top-level C/C++ `TEST(name) {…}`, `TEST(suite, name)`, `TEST_F`, `TEST_CASE(…)`-style heads are function boundaries, so editing or appending one test no longer stales its siblings. A macro head or invocation directly below the annotation (`TEST(n)`, `DEFINE_X(n, …)`, Rust `case!(n, …)`) supplies the exact test name (second argument for `TEST/TEST_F/TEST_P/TYPED_TEST/SCENARIO`). File-scope registration macro lines (`REG(fn);`, `CASE(suite, fn);`, one uppercase macro per line naming a function of the file) belong to the function they name (#236), and comments outside every function are not hashed. Known limit: an X-macro list on one line (`X(test_a) X(test_b)`) or a runner table is shared code outside every test body, so editing it stales every test in the file.
- PHP traits (#222): `use Trait;` inside a test class (or a local ancestor) joins the oracle closure like a parent class; such statements are no longer mistaken for namespace imports.
- PHP impact (#222): `use function` / `use const` (plain, aliased and group forms) resolve to the files declaring the namespaced function/const.
- JS/TS impact (#213): package.json `imports` (`#alias`, `#alias/*`, scoped to their package), `exports` wildcard subpaths (`./*`, `./feat/*`) and tsconfig `paths` star aliases to directories containing `index.ts` resolve to real files.
- `tdd merge-ledger` (#213): the leading intact, chained ledger lines stay byte-identical; only entries after the conflict are re-chained (same key order as normal appends).
- R impact (#224): literal `source("x.R")`, `sys.source(...)` and `source(file.path("a", "x.R"))` edges (relative to the file or the project root) are import-graph edges.
- Rust impact (#217): `#[path = "x.rs"] mod name;` maps `crate::name` importers to the real file.
- plan.md (#218): `—`/`–` in the depends column means "none"; C# impact extracts `record struct`/`record class` type names.

### Known limits not fixed in wave 3/4 (dogfood-7)
- Impact: dynamic R `source()` arguments (non-literal paths, `here::here`) are not followed; run `gate` without `--changed` when relying on them.
- `tdd stub` gaps: Python namespace dirs, C# `global using`, PHP functions/enums, R helper shadowing, C++ using-declarations (#214, #218, #222, #223, #224).
- Java (#216): a test declared in an `abstract class` runs through its single concrete subclass (`-Dtest=ImplTest#name`); zero or several concrete subclasses are refused as ambiguous/unresolved. A message-less exception (`java.lang.NullPointerException`) is shown as the `fails with:` reason.
- Timeouts (#226): test commands run in their own process group; on `timeoutMs` the whole group (launcher and hung test binary) is killed and the run is rejected with "test timed out after N ms (hung test?)".
- Workspace listing (#228): tracked files deleted from the working tree but not staged are dropped from the listing instead of crashing with ENOENT.
- Go (#215, #227): `Fuzz*` (seed corpus), `Benchmark*` (run once with `-bench ^Name$ -benchtime=1x`) and `Example*` functions can carry `@id`. A test file with `//go:build tag` is run with `-tags tag` automatically unless `testCmd` already has `-tags`; `[no test files]` rejections hint at build constraints. Go `tdd stub` field/method collisions are handled by the stub work, not here.
- Test-file siblings (#229): a sibling file that holds its own annotated tests (e.g. another part of a partial test class) contributes only its non-test content to the oracle hash, so appending a test there does not stale tests in this file; editing its shared content still does.
- PHPUnit (#222): a sibling's broken data provider (`There was 1 PHPUnit error`) is not the target's Red; tests declared in an abstract class or trait run through the concrete subclass(es) that extend/use them (rejected when none exists).
- C/C++ (#221): the first `tdd red/green` after a clean build no longer fails with "changed while running" when only the build-generated `compile_commands.json` context moved; an edit to the test file itself is still refused.
- Julia (#223): a macro-generated `@test` (reported at the macro definition's line) is credited to the test whose body contains its call-site stack frame, so `fails with:` and `--expect` see it.
- ExUnit: the oracle closure of a `*_test.exs` includes `test/test_helper.exs`, `test/support/**` and `Code.require_file`/`import_file` targets; `impact` follows `alias`/`import`/`use`/`require` (and aliased `Mod.fun` calls) to the files that `defmodule` the module.
- plan.md (#240): the depends column is separated by commas and/or whitespace (`a, b` or `a b`).
- Stale-evidence attribution (#236/#239): ledger entries record per-dependency hashes (`oracleShas`); `gate` ("test changed since last Green/Refactor — oracle dependency changed: <files>") and the `tdd green` refusal name the changed header/helper (the guard is per test; an edited production header that is not annotated `@id CODE-` is part of the oracle) and suggest `tdd red <ID> --retest "<reason>"`. `gate --verbose` lists every unproven test instead of the first 6. Not changed: header-only implementations still need an `@id CODE-` annotation to be excluded from the oracle; older ledger entries have no `oracleShas` and get no attribution.
- Java CSV oracles (#238): `@CsvFileSource(files=...)` resolves against the nearest `pom.xml`/`build.gradle` above the test (surefire cwd) even when `projects[].root` is the reactor; a `files=` path that does not exist is refused. Not covered: a runtime-opened data file (C `fopen(VECTORS_DIR "/x.csv")`) is invisible to the oracle hash and `projects[].dependsOn` only scopes `gate --changed`; `#include` a generated data header or run `tdd refactor` after vector edits.
- PHPUnit (#237): the Red `fails with:` text skips stack `file.php:N` lines, so a helper/trait assertion still shows `Failed asserting that ...`; `Premature end of PHP process` and `Allowed memory size ... exhausted` count as a crashed runner (Red/Green REJECTED, like other host crashes). Set `memory_limit` in phpunit.xml for runaway-recursion tests; children are killed with the process group on timeout (#226).
- node:test (#225): a Red where the only failing entry is the test file itself (module-level throw, nothing registered or executed) is recorded as a weak Red (load/setup), like a pytest collection error (#123); keep fixtures inside the test body or pass `--expect <text>`.
- JS stub (#219): CommonJS `require('./x.cjs')` of an existing module appends missing names as throwing stubs plus `module.exports.x = x`.
- Go stub (#215): when the compiler reports `cannot use F(..) (value of interface type any) as *pkg.T value`, the stub's F returns that type (also `[]*T`), creating the type when missing.
- ExUnit stub: a module the test `use`s gets `defmacro __using__(_opts)` (appended to an existing stub-only module), so `use MyApp.Case` compiles.
- C/C++ header-only implementations (#236): a header under `include/`, `src/`, `lib/` or `inc/` (and outside any `test*`, `fixtures`, `data`, `vectors`, `support` directory) is implementation, not oracle: editing it no longer refuses Green. Put `// @oracle` in such a header (or keep it in a test/data directory) to hash it as an oracle; `@id CODE-` annotation still works. Ledgers recorded before this change still match.
- `tdd refactor` (#239): when the test file's own region is unchanged but an oracle dependency (header, enum file, helper) moved, the warning names it (`oracle dependency changed since the last Green: <files>`) instead of "test body changed".
- Runtime data oracles (#238): `projects[].dependsOn` only scopes `gate --changed`. To make a data file part of a test's evidence, write `// @data path[, path2]` (relative to the test/oracle file or the repo root; a directory hashes every file in it) in the test or any oracle file it includes, or list repo-relative paths in `.sdd/config.json` `oracleData: ["vectors"]` (applies to every test). A changed or deleted file stales Green and names the path.
- PHPUnit/Pest orphans (#237): a test command naming `phpunit`/`pest` runs with a watchdog in its process group that kills the group when sdd itself dies (SIGKILL/terminal close); on timeout the group is killed as before. Still set `memory_limit` in phpunit.xml: the default CLI limit is unlimited.
- Round 5 notes (#244-#248): weak-Red setup detection follows helpers that reach the stub through other helpers, and treats a Go `if err := sut(..); err != nil` initializer as asserted. A Go goroutine panic that kills the test binary counts as a failing run of the test that was running. Data files read by tests (golden/fixtures) are not hashed into Red/Green evidence: review them by hand. `impact` on a data file is outside the import graph; use `gate --changed` (honours `projects[].dependsOn`) after editing shared fixtures. `tdd stub` for Elixir expands `alias A.{B, C}`, creates no empty modules for alias-only names, treats umbrella `apps/*/lib` modules and modules defined in the test file as existing, counts piped arguments and collapses trailing keyword pairs into one argument. C stubs search the nearest project root (CMakeLists/compile_commands) for `include/`, `src/` and `build/compile_commands.json`. Java stubs ignore upper-case constants declared in the test file.
- Stale-evidence (#264/#265): config `artifacts` files consumed by a test (listed under that test or one of its oracle files) are hashed into its oracle, so editing one between Red and Green is refused and after Green it stales the gate (existing ledgers of such tests need a fresh Red/`--retest`). `tdd green` warns when an `@implements` block (function/region; whole file if undelimitable; mtime for ledger entries lacking `implBlocks`) shared with other REQs changed after their Green/Refactor (post-Green production edits stay allowed). A support file that newly became an oracle dependency since Red (e.g. a stub-annotated file replaced without `@id CODE-`) is named in the REFUSED message with an annotation hint.
- Wave-10 (#267/#275/#276): a changed file of a config `parity` pair adds its peer to the `--changed` scope. Config `deliverables: ["contract/plan.json"]` marks an `artifacts` file as the deliverable itself: it is not hashed into the oracle, so a normal (non-weak) Red works and writing it does not stale other tests. Only table rows define REQs (a `- REQ-X:` bullet for an already-defined REQ is a reference). `[src: path:line]` annotations are checked by `trace` (missing file / line past EOF = warning); annotate code with `@id/@implements` BEFORE the first characterization Red, since adding ownership later invalidates it. `tdd green` and `impact REQ-X` signal a missing `@implements`.
- Wave-11 (#283): a bare stub call sharing an argument with the call whose bound result is asserted is the act, not setup; `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable` on a module-level `NAME = None` stub is setup-origin (weak); a Python `TypeError` about a function defined in the test file is rejected as a test bug; a matcher-less `assert.throws`/`pytest.raises(Exception)` that passes against the stub is rejected as vacuous; a module-level stub failure (node:test) prints a loud note; `--retest` after only an oracle artifact changed (test text identical) keeps the earlier strong Red (`testSha0` in the ledger).
- Rust doc tests (#287): put `/// @id TEST-.. @verifies REQ-..` in the doc comment directly above (or inside the same `///` block as) a ``` fence. `tdd red/green` resolves the exact `cargo test --doc` name (`path - item (line N)`, from `--list`, one fence per marker) and runs only that test (substring filter; rustdoc ignores `--exact`); evidence hashes only that `///` block, so editing the implementation keeps the Red valid. `trace`/`gate` count the ID like any other `@id`. Not covered: several fences under one `@id`, `//!` inner docs used as oracle for module-level items beyond the block, `tdd stub` for doc tests, doc-test-aware `{changedCargoPkgs}` scoping.
- Wave 12 (#294): `impact` follows a config `parity` pair one hop (counterpart file and its feature; the counterpart's importers are not added). For a non-code artifact it prints `producers:` (build.rs / codegen / generator files, or files that write the artifact and name it). `impact --all` disables the `+N more` truncation.
- Wave 14 (#308): `impact A B …` reports every target (one `--json` line each); producer detection also recognises `open(…, "w")`, `write_bytes`, `to_json`/`to_csv`.
- Tracker #309 (r21a): the per-`@implements`-block hash ignores comment-only nested `@id CODE-…` annotation lines inside the block, so editing a nested annotation no longer stales the outer block (hash unchanged for blocks without nested annotations, so existing ledgers stay valid). Not changed: #265 (already refuses with the production-ownership message; no minimal repro of the setup-only edit left), refusal-loop hints, artifact invalidation, T1 re-approval and shared-preamble staling need staleness-model design decisions.
- Wave-15 (#309): `(characterization)` on a REQ row is a spec-level waiver like `(test-only)`: no first-Green "no code carries @implements" warning, no missing-`@implements` warning, passing Red is recorded as characterization. Without the marker the warning stays (#286). `[src:]` now also accepts `path:N-M` and an optional backticked anchor (`[src: a.ts:10-20 \`fn\`]`); `trace` warns (never errors) when the range does not resolve, the cited lines are all blank, or the anchor text is absent from them. `--retest` keeps its decision: a retest that still fails is already an ordinary strong Red; one that passes is a weak Red superseding the strong one (with warning) — not changed. SUT-as-setup, Go/ExUnit receiver weak-Red unification and Java weak-Red are deliberately not changed (no minimal repro / needs redesign / no JUnit).
- Refusal/stale hints (#309 r22a, messages only; what is stale/refused is unchanged): the cause is classified and the hint names only a command that would be accepted. A shared/preamble-only edit (the test's own lines unchanged) → `tdd refactor <ID>` (on T1 with `--wording "<why>"`, which must be non-empty; an empty one is called out); an edit of the test's own lines → `tdd red <ID> --retest "<reason>"`; before Green, a shared-only edit → a fresh Red (`tdd red <ID>`), never `--retest`; implementation/ownership change → a fresh Red.

## Spec-edit re-approval and `--review` (#309)
- `specEditPolicy: "reapprove"` (config.md): T1 `tdd refactor` of a REQ whose row changed since its Green needs `--wording <why>`; default is the old warning.
- `approve record --review`: an empty value is refused for every approver; a value that looks like a file path (absolute, `./`, or `*.md/.markdown/.txt`) but does not exist is refused for humans as well as AI. Free-text summaries (e.g. `no findings`) and omitting the flag for humans still work.
- Tracker #309 artifact staleness (opt-in `artifactStaleness: true`): a declared `artifacts` file referenced by name from a test is hashed into Green/Refactor evidence; a later change makes `gate` report the evidence stale naming the artifact. Older entries (no `artifactShas`) are unaffected.
- Tracker #312 (r23c): `tdd refactor --stale` includes artifact-stale tests; opt-in `artifactGranularity: "test"` narrows artifact staleness per test; Cargo workspace `members` globs are expanded for gate attribution and `impact`; `impact` of a declared artifact lists only its readers. Not changed: the differing remedy text for T1 (`--wording`) stays, as a T1 `refactor` needs a reason by design.
- Tracker #309 (r22d, #300): opt-in `.sdd/config.json` `preambleGranularity: "symbol"` narrows shared-preamble staling for TS/JS, Python and Rust: imports/declarations still stale every test, a top-level helper/fixture edit stales only tests that reference it (transitively). Default (field absent) is unchanged.
- Wave-23 (#311, r23b): the Red record for a `(characterization)` REQ now says `(characterization) REQ` (`(test-only) REQ` only for that marker). The setup-call weak-Red advice now also names the real fix when the failing call is the stubbed/act call itself (`--expect` cannot help): stub it with a minimal working body, or `--allow-setup-red`. Deliberately NOT changed (heuristic/ambiguous, no safe minimal fix): setup-vs-act classification differences between helper-wrapped and direct calls and under `stubThrowingConstructors`, act-call-as-setup false positives (use `--allow-setup-red`), Red "fails with" text selection (assert message/cleanup/predicate), and `--retest` (already tagged `retest`/weak and listed by the gate; superseding a strong Red already warns).
- Tracker #314 (r23e): Red of a `(characterization)` REQ prints `(characterization) REQ`, a `(test-only)` REQ keeps `(test-only) REQ`. `approve <feature>` (no subcommand) names the missing subcommand. The gate evidence note for refactor-recorded tests says `--retest` + Green replaces it. Decisions: `gate` appends to `.sdd/tdd.jsonl` only for a `flaky` retry (the output now says so; commit it) — no opt-out added; flaky retry stays limited to the gate `test` check (`tdd green` is never retried); `[src:]` anchor drift stays a trace warning (no `--strict-src`). Skipped: Green-after-header-change text (a #309 test requires that a header-only refusal does not suggest --retest); skipped as risky: making `tdd refactor` clear the "no new Red" evidence note.
- Tracker r24a (design 3.1, fail-closed gate): `gate --changed` prints `scope: exact=N widened=N unknown=N`; changed files claimed by nothing are `unknown` and, under `scopePolicy: "strict"` (written by `init` for new configs; absent key = `warn`), fail the gate with the file list. Waivers: config `unscoped` globs, `--allow-unscoped <glob>` (ledger `scope-waiver`), default ignores `**/*.md`, `.github/**`, `LICENSE`, `.sdd/**`. Workspace-root Cargo/JS/Python manifests, lockfiles and toolchain files widen to all projects of that ecosystem. Not done: widening for ecosystems without a project mapping, and a per-file closure for root checks.
- Tracker r25c (design 3.1/3.3/3.5): `gate --json` has `tdd: {weak:[ids], suspect:[ids]}`. `gate --changed --explain` prints per check `scope` (exact|widened|skipped), closure size, first 10 members and why each changed file was or was not claimed (also `scope.explain` in `--json`; default output unchanged). Root `go.mod/go.sum/go.work`, `pom.xml/build.gradle*/settings.gradle*`, `mix.exs/mix.lock`, `*.csproj/*.sln/Directory.Build.props` widen to the projects of that ecosystem; with no such project they stay `unknown` (warn, or fail under `scopePolicy: "strict"`). Not done: `review` has no weak-Red output, so nothing to expose there.
- Dogfood stop criterion (design 3.5): classify each finding S1 (crash, gate false-pass, wrong Green accepted, data loss), S2 (wrong Red/stub that blocks with no workaround) or S3 (heuristic miss with a documented workaround, message quality). A wave must have S1 = S2 = 0; **two consecutive waves with S1 = S2 = 0 end the loop**. S3 findings go into one tracker Issue and are fixed only when they reproduce twice.
- Tracker r24d (design 3.4, self-verification; tests only, no tool change): `sdd.test.mjs` ends with (1) a scope differential per ecosystem (Cargo/JS/Python fixtures, fake hash-of-inputs checks as oracle: every single-file mutation must keep `gate --changed` scope ⊇ the checks whose result changed; unclaimed file warns, fails under strict), (2) a Rust stub round-trip (each generated const/type is evidence-typed or carries `SDD-TODO(stub)` and is listed by `tdd stub --report`; compiles under cargo or carries a marker; no cargo = counted `SKIP: toolchain missing`), (3) ledger invariants on rechained tdd.jsonl fixtures (Red before Green, no Green on stale evidence, merge-ledger idempotent). Known gaps are recorded as `todo` tests named `r24d TODO stub:` (untyped call returns emitted as `i64` without marker, free fns absent from `--report`, float-compared method stubbed `-> i64`, loop-bound const element types guessed `i64`); not fixed (heuristic long tail, risky).

## Gate fail-open audit (r25b)

Audit of `gate` paths that could end PASS (exit 0) with missing or unverifiable evidence (classes per docs/design-sdd-hardening.md §3.5). Repros are in `sdd.test.mjs` (`r25b …`).

| Path | Repro | Class | Fix / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changedCmd` check, only deleted files changed | delete `lib.mjs`, `gate --changed` | S1 | skipped as "no changed files" and passed. Now runs the full check (`only deleted files changed`) |
| Root test check skipped because all changes are in a nested project that has no checks | `projects:[{root:'app'}]`, root `test` check, edit `app/x.mjs` | S1 | nothing ran. `scopePolicy` strict: `✗` fail; warn (default for existing configs): `!` line naming the project |
| Unclaimed changed file (no project / dependsOn / check) | r24a | — | already handled by r24a (`scopePolicy`, `unscoped`, `--allow-unscoped`, ledger) |
| `--changed` with a bad `--baseline` ref | `--baseline nope` | none | REFUSED, exit 2 |
| git unavailable / `git status` or `git diff` fails | non-repo root | none | falls back to full evidence and checks, not "no changes" |
| Configured command missing (ENOENT) | `cmd:["nonexistent"]` | none | exit 127 → `✗` fail |
| Check ran zero tests / all skipped / scoped run matched no tests | `node --test` with no files | none | exit 2 INCOMPLETE; scoped zero-test run re-runs the full check |
| No spec / `--no-run` / no commands configured | — | none | INCOMPLETE (exit 2), never PASS |
| Failing check downgraded | flaky retry | S3 | `flaky.policy: "warn"` accepts a pass-on-rerun; opt-in, recorded as a `flaky` ledger entry |
| Hub change that is comment/whitespace-only skips the hub fallback | symbol-neutral edit | S3 | semantically a no-op; printed as `!` |
| Changed `.sdd/**` (e.g. config edit) not treated as a change for `changedCmd` | edit `.sdd/config.json` | S3 | `.sdd/**` is a default scope ignore; lock/ledger/approval checks always run |
| Approval/lock absent | T2 or `approval: human` without lock | none | `✗ lock` fail; spec removal also fails |
| Stale evidence accepted | edit test/REQ/oracle after Green | none | `evidenceStatus` fails (hash of REQ, test region and oracle deps); changed oracles pull their REQs into `--changed` scope |
| `prepare` step cached on unchanged inputs | — | none | key covers cmd + input hashes + outputs exist |
